title: REDI-NET FV-2 Flying Vector Processing
author: REDI-NET Consortium
materials: Select the program IndiMag_Pathogen_KF_Flex_4wash on the instrument.
Select program IndiMag_Pathogen_KF_Duo_4wash on the instrument.
APPENDIX 4. MS35BE ELECTROSTATIC DISCHARGE PROTECTION MODEL
Use gloves while handling the tray.
Lens cleaner, glass cleaner or ethanol

steps.title: Sort Flying Vector Samples
steps.instruction: Sort flying vectors by species, collection date, and collection location. Optionally sort by trap type. Only female flying vectors should be processed for testing.

steps.title: Set Up Mosquitoes e-ID (Bluetooth)
steps.instruction: Configure the Agamotto device via Bluetooth using a computer or phone with Google Chrome.

substeps.instruction: Plug in the device.
Visit https://mos-id.vectech.io and log in (sign up if first time).
Click the drop-down arrow at the top-center, select 'Add New Device', and click the Bluetooth icon.
Select 'Agamotto' and click 'Pair'.
Enter Wi-Fi credentials when prompted.
Return to the 'Data' tab, click the drop-down arrow, and verify the status is [Idle]. If [booting], wait until it changes to [idle].

steps.title: Set Up Mosquitoes e-ID (Ethernet)
steps.instruction: Configure the device using an Ethernet connection if Bluetooth is not used.

substeps.instruction: Select the user menu at the bottom right and select 'Connect Device'.
Select 'Device' and choose the Wi-Fi name from the 'Wi-Fi SSD' drop-down menu.
Enter the Wi-Fi password and select connect.
Power-cycle the device by disconnecting from power and ethernet, then reconnecting power.
If status does not change to [Idle], connect an Ethernet cable directly from the device to the modem.

steps.title: Image Specimens Using Mosquitoes e-ID
steps.instruction: Capture dorsal and ventral images of specimens while maintaining the cold chain (dry ice or polystyrene boxes with cool beans).

substeps.instruction: Navigate to the 'Trays' tab on https://mos-id.vectech.io and verify the device is plugged in.
Organize specimens in sample tubes in a 96-well sample rack (8x12).
Place a glass tray on the chill table and lay out specimens sequentially (e.g., A1-A12) dorsal side up. Ensure specimens are dry.
Close the tray lid until the magnets click and insert the tray into the device slot.
Click 'Capture New Tray' to capture the dorsal view.
Enter Genus, species, plate, and well number (A1-H12) in the data fields.
Remove the tray, flip it upside down (ventral side up), re-insert, and click 'Capture Other Side'.
Click 'Finish' and return specimens to original storage. Note the tray number.

steps.title: Prepare DinoScope
steps.instruction: Set up the DinoScope hardware and stage for high-resolution imaging.

substeps.instruction: Place a portable chill table on the adjustable stand.
Place a white porcelain stage (or a 5 cm x 5 cm paper note card attached to a petri dish) on the chill table and secure it with tape.
Adjust the DinoScope holster to be 4.5 cm above the stage surface and secure the rear set screw.
Turn on the chill table and wait for the surface temperature to reach -20 °C.
Clean the stage surface with a Kimwipe and 75% ethanol (or replace paper cards).
Ensure specimens are in individual Eppendorf tubes in labeled 96-well racks.

steps.title: Image Specimens Using DinoScope
steps.instruction: Capture detailed dorsal and ventral images of a representative specimen from each pool.

substeps.instruction: Use forceps to place a specimen in the center of the stage, dorsal side up.
Focus and center the specimen using the interface and fine adjustment.
Set the correct magnification and ensure metadata (magnification, profile, scale, username, annotation) is included and not overlapping the specimen.
Annotate using the convention: Sample ID-View (e.g., RUSFV-00001D).
Readjust white balance immediately before taking the image.
Capture the image and review for quality; repeat if unsatisfactory.
Flip the specimen to the ventral side and repeat the imaging process.
Return the specimen to the tube and repeat for all specimens.
Copy and save photos from the dated folder.

steps.title: Prepare for Flying Vector Homogenization
steps.instruction: Prepare reagents and equipment to prevent contamination and ensure efficient lysis.

substeps.instruction: Pre-cool the Bullet Blender by adding dry ice to the cooling compartment and running the cooling program.
Clean work surfaces with RNaseZap, then wipe with 70% molecular biology grade ethanol.
Transfer two spoons (approx. 200 µL) of 0.1 mm zirconium oxide beads into Clear RINO 1.5 mL screw-cap tubes.
For first-time use of IndiMag pathogen kit: add 100% ethanol to Buffer AW1 and AW2, and 100% Isopropanol to ACB.
Warm Buffer ATL to 56 °C if precipitates are present. Prepare Buffer ATL-DX by adding 100 µL Reagent DX to 15 mL Buffer ATL (or 10 µL Reagent DX to 1.5 mL Buffer ATL).
Vortex MagAttract Suspension G for 3 minutes (first use) or 1 minute (subsequent uses).
Prepare 15 mL or 50 mL conical tubes with nuclease-free water for TNA elution.

steps.title: Homogenize Flying Vectors
steps.instruction: Mechanically disrupt the mosquito samples using the Bullet Blender.

substeps.instruction: Clean forceps with 70% ethanol and Kimwipes.
Label navy RINO RNA lysis tubes on the cap.
Transfer ≤20 individuals into the RINO tube, add 400 µL cold sterile 1xPBS, and place on ice.
Load tubes into the cooled Bullet Blender.
Set controls to Speed 10 and Time 3, then press Start.
Centrifuge the suspension at 100 x g, 4 °C, for 1 minute to pellet debris.
Carefully transfer the top 320 µL of supernatant into 1.5 mL tubes.

steps.title: Perform Microbe Lysis
steps.instruction: Further lyse the homogenate using beads and the Bullet Blender.

substeps.instruction: Add 80 µL of ATL-DX Lysis Buffer and 0.1 mm beads to 1.5 mL tubes; label with sample/pool ID.
Prepare a positive control: 37.5 µL ZymoBIOMICS Microbial Community Standard Material and 282.5 µL 1x PBS (total 320 µL).
Prepare a negative control: 320 µL cold sterile 1xPBS.
Transfer 320 µL of homogenate (or control) into the pre-labeled bead tubes.
Load tubes into the cooled Bullet Blender, set speed to 12 and time to 3, and press Start.
Let samples settle for 1 minute, then repeat the beating process (Step 62).
Centrifuge at 120 x g, 4 °C, for 5 minutes.
Transfer 350 µL of supernatant to a new snap-cap 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube. (Optional: store at 4 °C overnight).

steps.title: TNA Extraction (KingFisher Flex)
steps.instruction: Extract total nucleic acids using the KingFisher Flex instrument.

substeps.instruction: Load the program 'IndiMag_Pathogen_KF_Flex_4wash'.
Set up plates: Elution (75 µL nuclease-free water), Wash 1 (700 µL Buffer AW1), Wash 2 (700 µL Buffer AW2), Wash 3 (750 µL 80% ethanol), Wash 4 (750 µL 100% ethanol), and Tip Comb (96 Deep-well).
Add 20 µL Proteinase K to a new Deep-well plate; transfer 270 µL of supernatant from the lysis step into these wells (Sample Plate).
Prepare a master mix (with 10% overage) of 135 µL Buffer VXL, 540 µL Buffer ACB, and 20 µL MagAttract Suspension G per sample. Mix for 2 min on Hula mixer and add 695 µL to each sample.
Start the run and load plates when prompted.
After ~35 minutes, remove the elution plate and cover or transfer eluate to storage tubes.

steps.title: TNA Extraction (KingFisher Duo Prime)
steps.instruction: Extract total nucleic acids using the KingFisher Duo Prime instrument.

substeps.instruction: Load the program 'IndiMag_Pathogen_KF_Duo_4wash' and confirm 12-tip magnetic heads and 12-well heat blocks are used.
Set up the Sample Plate: Row A (985 µL Lysate/buffer), Row B (700 µL Buffer AW1), Row C (700 µL Buffer AW2), Row D (750 µL 80% ethanol), Row E (750 µL 100% ethanol), Row F (Tip comb 700 µL).
Set up the Elution Strip: Row A (75 µL nuclease-free water).
Add 20 µL Proteinase K to the sample row; transfer 270 µL of supernatant from the lysis step into these wells.
Prepare and add a master mix (with 10% overage) of 135 µL Buffer VXL, 540 µL Buffer ACB, and 20 µL MagAttract Suspension G (695 µL total per sample).
Start the run and load the plate/strip. Keep the door open during extraction to prevent ethanol vapor contamination.
After ~35 minutes, remove the elution strip and transfer eluate to storage.

steps.title: Quantify and Store TNA
steps.instruction: Measure DNA/RNA concentrations and store samples according to duration.

substeps.instruction: For DNA: Mix 1 µL sample with 199 µL 1x HS dsDNA Qubit Assay in a 0.6 mL tube.
For RNA: Prepare working solution (199 µL Qubit RNA HS Assay buffer + 1 µL Dye per sample). Mix 199 µL working solution with 1 µL sample and incubate for 1 minute at room temperature.
Measure concentrations using a Qubit 4 Fluorometer.
Store samples at -20 °C for <2 weeks or -80 °C for long-term storage.

steps.title: Clean and Maintain IDX Tray
steps.instruction: Clean the imaging tray every 10 captures or when debris/smudges are visible.

substeps.instruction: Remove screws and set tray walls aside.
Apply lens cleaner to the glass and wipe with a Kimwipe or microfiber cloth until dry and clear (top and bottom of base and cover).
Inspect glass against a light source and clean remaining smudges.
Reinstall tray walls (indentations facing gold inserts) and replace screws.
